body:
# the contributor audit: convex-threshold approximate cap coverage

Audited source: `candidate 2623b39acd3d4a1d`, Sections 1--9, 2026-09-25.

**PASS, within the explicit threshold premise.** This does not prove that every critical cap family has a sufficiently inexpensive threshold.

1. The intrinsic dimension is an integer: the maximum affine dimension of the finitely many nonempty compact convex integer fibers. Each maximal-dimensional fiber has positive finite normalized Hausdorff measure; smaller ones have zero measure. Finite Borel additivity gives the exact fiber sum. There is no use of ambient volume.

2. An uncovered section is the intersection of a compact convex fiber with finitely many open halfspaces. It is convex, Borel, and bounded, though not necessarily closed. Positive intrinsic measure forces affine dimension at least q. Relative interiors justify every dimension calculation without closure changes.

3. For two positive residuals, their Minkowski average has dimension greater than q if either residual has dimension greater than q or their q-dimensional direction spaces differ. Its H_q is then infinite. If both direction spaces coincide, translation into a common Euclidean q-space permits ordinary Brunn--Minkowski. Thus the strict superlevel above the qth power of any finite nonnegative convex threshold is convex. No Brunn--Minkowski inequality in nonparallel q-planes is asserted.

4. The positive integer base set is same-parity midpoint closed. An average with dimension greater than q at an integer midpoint would contradict the definition of q. The already proved finite occupied-parity Helly theorem therefore applies to the convex, possibly nonclosed strict superlevels. It selects at most k residual sets. Taking the union of their at-most-t ORIGINAL cap index sets gives at most kt caps, and preserves the threshold bound pointwise at every measured integer fiber.

5. The cap budget is exactly kt B >= M - sum ell(p)^q. In particular t=2 and q=d=2 require residual cost at most M/9 to give B >= 4M/(9k). Since k<=2^n, the last conversion has the correct direction. The theorem does not require or imply that this residual cost bound always holds.

6. The affine-majorant optimization is attained in the finite vector space of sampled affine values. For hinge thresholds, the auxiliary nonnegative T variables and elimination of affine coefficients give a closed polyhedral feasible projection. Objective sublevels in T are compact. A feasible affine preimage exists at the attained minimizer, and replacing T by its actual positive part cannot increase the objective. Negative affine values at zero-residual sites cause no gap.

7. Closed caps are used throughout; their open complements are exact set complements. Positive boundary mass is never discarded. All normals may couple integer and continuous coordinates. No transformation of the lattice is used.

8. q=0 is treated separately by exact projected residual sets. Every nonempty fiber is then a singleton. There are no zero-th roots or 0^0 conventions in the proof. The counting cap budget M/k follows from a k-cap subcover of any given finite covering family.

The remaining interface is quantitative, not a technical limit: the approximate-cover conclusion needs an explicit global convex threshold with controlled total cost. Small residuals on only part of the fibers do not supply that premise.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
